_doc: The traders (economy refactor 2026-10-17, ECONOMY_REFACTOR_PROPOSAL D3-D7). Read by src/traders.py (pure: the plan, the stock, the offers, the deeds prices) and src/game_traders.py (the Game side: placing them, the shop's Buy / Sell / Services tabs). Each trader is a person with a name, a reason to be down here and a few short lines; none of them is a vending machine. Their goods are a one-time chance: no restock. Stock stays unidentified and is priced by what it is WORTH (data/item_worth.json), so a sharp eye can price-identify. They BUY at 20-25% of their own price (half of it, on a visit when the hero buys from them, up to what he spends: the trade-in), up to what is in their purse, never quest pieces, never anything worn, and a thing bought from any trader never sells back for more than half of what was paid (no buy/sell loop). Services sell a second chance, never the answer. Since the winning build (3.5, 2026-11-13) they also help a build: part of every shelf counters what walks the floors below (counters), smiths reforge, silver and inlay, armourers line a cloak or shirt and take special orders, and an altar rededicates (src/rededication.py).

friend_lines._doc: What a friend says at his host's stall (traders.friend_lines): plain enough for any of the six. His own entry gives his lore, greeting ('line') and counter, and may give 'lines' of his own over these. He never says his host's. 'reaction' stands in for the host's line when a rumour moves his price.
friend_lines.bought: My thanks, and may it serve you well.
friend_lines.sold: It's a bargain, and I'll find someone who has need of it.
friend_lines.broke: I'm sorry, but I can't let it go for less.
friend_lines.refuse: I don't deal in that kind of thing.
friend_lines.purse_empty: My purse is empty, so I can buy no more.
friend_lines.sold_out: That is all that I have to sell.
friend_lines.order_placed: Your {item} will be ready for you at the stall on floor {floor}.
friend_lines.order_ready: Here is your {item}, made as you ordered.
friend_lines.order_refund: There's no stall of mine below this one, so have your coin back.
friend_lines.reaction: I have heard what is told of your dealings, and my prices go by it.

always_stocked.why: The lethal petrifiers (basilisks, gorgons) begin on floor 25, and every gate camp stands on 19, 39, 59 and 79: the cure is always for sale before stone can kill (Brandon, 2026-11-22: counters always obtainable).

plan._doc: Which floors get a trader, rolled once a run from the Road's seed (road.rng_for), never from the shared random stream. Gate camps stand on the floor before each gate boss, always. Specialists take 'count' floors inside their range; then each floor left takes the generalist who keeps to it (the 'generalists' list, each with its own floors) with 'generalist_chance'. A trader avoids the Emberpup's and the Black Knight's floors and prefers floors with no anchor, medium or high Road slot; he never stands on a boss floor, floor 1, 99 or 100, or the Cow Level. Depth-true (Brandon, 2026-11-12): every range keeps inside the reach of the being who trades there (the 'reach' table below; tests/test_depth_true.py). 'generalist' and 'generalist_floors' are the pre-list keys: traders.generalists still reads them when 'generalists' is absent.

reach._doc: How deep each kind of being can go (Brandon, 2026-11-12: "as we descend, it feels like we are delving deeper and deeper, to places where normal men cannot go"; _alive_research/ENCOUNTER_AUDIT.md, reach table). Every trader and friend here names its 'reach', and so does every Road anchor in data/npc_encounters.json (its person's 'reach': the most limited being the scene puts there). tests/test_depth_true.py holds every one of their floors inside these. The five domains: 1-20 the Labyrinth, 21-40 the Forgotten Temple, 41-60 the Scorched Deep, 61-80 the Rime Halls, 81-100 the Abyss.

ordinary.who: Ordinary folk: townsfolk, farmers, children, aldermen. No one who has sought the deep has returned, and their own lines point up to the town.

hardy.who: Hardy delvers: soldiers, knights, guild mapmakers, armed pilgrims, slavers and bandits. Mortal guards, mobs and bandits stop spawning by about 45.

exceptional.who: The exceptional mortal: a Legion company at the very edge, an armourer who stayed where an army vanished.

called.who: Mortals carried by a holy calling, rare by design: a prophet who went down on purpose, a paladin whose armour is still blessed.

deep_folk.who: Dwarves and deep gnomes. Fafnir was a dwarf, and the Scorched Deep's kin are dwarves gone wrong.

giants_fair_folk.who: Trolls, giants and the Fair Folk, who live under hills and under the ground at any depth to the frost.

dead.who: The dead, who stay where they died: ghosts, draugr, the shades of delvers.

captive.who: Captives and the possessed: carried down by something else, and as deep as it went.

immortal.who: Legends who cannot die, such as the Sibyl of Cumae, who led Aeneas down to the dead.

greek_god.who: Greek gods in disguise, in Athena's lost temple.

norse_god.who: Norse gods and their kin in disguise, in the Rime Halls on the eve of Ragnarok.

saint_angel.who: Saints and angels, anywhere: heaven's messengers go where they are sent.

deep_being.who: Things that are not men and only look it: Vesper, and Ambrose Vell, who does not breathe.

damned_demon.who: Demons and the damned, from the Rime Halls down: the Locust cultists, the rich man at the gulf.

stock_bias._doc: 2026-10-18, Brandon: "merchants should be an excellent way for kids to find or CHOOSE items they haven't yet encountered, helps to BUILD the character." Each random pick of a trader's stock is weighted toward kinds the hero has not held yet this run (Player.seen_item_ids): a kind he has held weighs seen_weight against 1. A gear pick draws gear_candidates pieces for the floor and keeps one by the same weights. Each trader's 'spread' lists groups of item classes; his stall always holds at least one ware from each group, so a kid can pick what suits the build. The lean picks KINDS only: wares are still sold unidentified, and their power is their own (weighted to the floor like any loot).

treasure._doc: Coin weight and treasure (Brandon's D2, 2026-10-18; src/treasure.py). Every trader buys treasure at buy_rate of its value (capped by his purse) and takes it as payment at the same rate when coin runs short, giving change from his purse. gem_stock: how many gems each kind of trader has for sale, at value x sell_markup: the coin-to-gem exchange. Gems are never haggled and never take a friend's or charity discount (a rise for a wronged guild still applies), so buying and selling them always loses.

rare_stock._doc: D8, Brandon: "No WIS purchase, possible rare shop appearance?" The Draught of Mimir's Well: +1 WIS for good, but drinking it asks a quiz (data/items/potion.json 'quiz'); a wrong answer wastes it. About 1 trader stock in 30, floor 40 and down; 'share' is its price in floors of income (economy.merchant_price).

repair.name: Mend Rust and Acid
repair.desc: Restores the enchantment rust, acid or fire ate off one worn piece. Never above what it had.

sharpen.name: Sharpen Your Weapon
sharpen.desc: +1 to the weapon in your hand. A smith will do this twice for any one blade, no more.

reinforce.name: Reinforce Your Armour
reinforce.desc: +1 to the armour on your body. Twice per piece, no more.

cut_curse.name: Cut Off a Cursed Thing
cut_curse.desc: Cuts away one cursed piece you cannot take off. The piece is destroyed; you keep the slot and your skin.

cure.name: Cure What Ails You
cure.desc: Poison, disease, blindness, confusion, stone, a hex, a charm, fear and the shakes: treated and gone.

restore.name: Restore Drained Strength
restore.desc: Every stat point a drain, a poison or a disease took off you, put back.

heal.name: Bind Your Wounds
heal.desc: Your wounds cleaned and bound: back to full health.

id_retry.name: Study an Item Together
id_retry.desc: Identify one item with a scribe at your elbow. You still answer the question; a wrong answer costs you nothing but the fee.

map.name: Buy a Map of This Floor
map.desc: The whole layout of this floor, inked.

porter.name: Hire a Porter
porter.desc: Someone carries part of your load for the next three floors.

reforge.name: Reforge Your Weapon
reforge.desc: Re-shapes the weapon in your hand into another of the same metal: a longsword into a mace. Its plus, its blessing and the smith's work stay with it.

silvering.name: Silver Your Weapon
silvering.desc: Works silver into the weapon in your hand, for good. It strikes as silver does, and the dead and the shapechangers cannot bear silver. One inlay to a weapon.

cold_iron_inlay.name: Inlay Cold Iron
cold_iron_inlay.desc: Works cold iron into the weapon in your hand, for good. It strikes as cold iron does, and the Fair Folk and demons cannot abide cold iron. One inlay to a weapon.

lining.name: Line a Cloak or Shirt
lining.desc: Lines the cloak or shirt you wear against fire, cold, lightning or poison: that harm does a quarter less to you. One lining to a piece.

special_order.name: Special Order
special_order.desc: Order a piece in the metal and shape you choose. Pay now; it waits for you at the smith's next stall, deeper down.

trade_in.name: Trade In
trade_in.desc: On a visit when you buy here or pay for a service, what you sell fetches half the trader's price instead of a fifth, up to what you spend.

counters._doc: Stock that knows what's below (winning build 3.5, Brandon 2026-11-13: "the dungeon needs to SUPPORT this through the merchants and altars"). src/domain_counters.py reads what spawns on the floors at and just below a stall ('span' floors past it), at run time, and ranks what those kinds are weak to ('weak': a form, a substance and holy are measured through combat.weapon_type_multiplier on a probe weapon; an element by the kind's own weaknesses) and what they hurt with ('guard': the type of their attacks). Each trader sets out up to 'per_stall' counters: the first offer HIS line can supply for the commonest weakness, then a guard for the commonest attack element if it touches at least 'guard_min_share' of what walks below (or the need's own 'min_share'). The named counters (slice 5, src/counters.py) are guards for a way of attacking rather than an element: 'delivery' is how the attacks land (gaze, voice; 'riders': only one that carries an effect), 'families'/'tags' with 'effects' a family's glamour. A gear counter (whose use shows on it) is marked as set out for what walks below; a wand, potion or book counter is not, so nothing is identified. 'foes' words the family most of the kinds belong to; his 'counter' line says it when the stall opens.

gaze.foes: eyes that turn men to stone are watching

voice.foes: things wail and sing in the dark

foes.aberrations: things with too many eyes crawl

inlays._doc: Silvering and the cold-iron inlay (src/smithing.py): the substance joins the weapon's damage_types, which the bane rule reads. 'prefix' goes on its name; 'card' is its Kit card line; 'done' is what the smith does.

silver.name: silver
silver.card: Silvered: it strikes as silver does, and the dead and the shapechangers cannot bear silver.
silver.done: {who} beats a skin of silver into your {name} and polishes it until it shines like the moon.

cold_iron.name: cold iron
cold_iron.card: Inlaid with cold iron: it strikes as cold iron does, and the Fair Folk and demons cannot abide it.
cold_iron.done: {who} hammers a vein of cold iron into your {name}, cold, never letting it near the fire.

linings._doc: Linings (src/smithing.py): one to a worn cloak or shirt, that element's damage x0.75 while it is worn (Player.get_armor_resistance). 'stuff' is what the armourer lines it with.

fire.name: Fire
fire.stuff: salamander's wool, the stone cloth that will not burn

lightning.name: Lightning
lightning.stuff: oiled silk, which lightning will not cross

guild._doc: D7. 'wronged': a merchant-type person the hero robbed or sold. The traders talk: their prices rise for the rest of the run, and the next one says why (once). No karma: it is the market, not God. 'credit': each oath the hero kept earns one thing free (up to a floor's income) at the next trader; word gets round. 'reactions': charity carries no karma but has consequences; each trader reacts by his own nature (data per trader).

rumours._doc: Conditions a trader's 'reactions' refer to by name (deeds.check conditions).

generalist.name: Grindle
generalist.title: Deep Gnome Trader
generalist.lore: Grindle is a small grey trader with a pack twice his size and a lantern that he never seems to need. He will not say where his stock comes from, save that the previous owners are past caring. He buys anything, cheaply, and he always speaks of himself by name, saying that this is the custom of gnomes, though it is no such thing.

lines.counter: Grindle hears that below here {foes}, and as luck has it, Grindle sells {take}.
greet: Grindle sells and Grindle buys, and Grindle never asks where you got it.
The previous owners are long past caring, so have a look.
Grindle's wares are all real, or most, or some of them.
You smell like a fight, and fights bring Grindle customers. Welcome!
lines.bought: A pleasure, and Grindle never saw you.
lines.sold: Done, but don't tell Grindle its story, for Grindle doesn't want to know.
lines.broke: No coin, no deal. Grindle likes you, but not so well as that.
lines.refuse: Grindle won't buy that, for even Grindle has standards, low though they be.
lines.purse_empty: Grindle's purse is empty, and it makes Grindle very sad.
lines.sold_out: That is all there is. Grindle's pack is light and Grindle's heart is glad.

reactions.line: Grindle hears you pay other people's debts. Grindle has debts, so prices go up.
So you're the soft touch that Wren's lot talk about? Ha! Then prices go up.

friend.counter: The word is that below here {foes}, so I have brought {take}, for you especially.
friend.name: Pomfrey Quill
friend.title: Alderman and Trader
friend.lore: Pomfrey Quill, alderman and collector, followed the adventurers down from the town because he thought there would be profit in it, and he sat in terror upon his trunk until you walked him to the stair. Now he has come down again to trade, in a coat as absurdly fine as ever, and he has not forgotten who brought him out alive.
friend.line: Pomfrey Quill, alderman, trader, and ALIVE, thanks to you! You shall have a friend's price on everything, and this time I mean it.

apothecary.name: Mother Wort
apothecary.title: Apothecary
apothecary.lore: Agnes Wort came down into the dark for the cave-moss that has never seen the sun, since it cures what the sun-moss cannot. Eleven years she has dwelt here, and she says that she will climb home again when the moss runs out, though in truth it never will.
apothecary._doc_flasks: Coatings and flasks (slice 5): one is always on her shelf (the spread). Beeswax for the ears now and then, and always when wailing things are below ('counter_classes': a counter, domain_counters).

lines.counter: Below here {foes}, dear, so take {take} and thank me later.
greet: Wipe your feet, dear, for you're bleeding on my moss.
Moss that's never seen the sun cures what the sun-moss can't, so don't touch that jar.
Sit and put your tongue out. Ugh! Well, let's see what we can do.
lines.bought: Drink it slowly, or you'll soon learn why I told you to.
lines.sold: I'll take it, for somebody down here always needs one.
lines.broke: I give no credit, dear, for that's how an apothecary ends up as moss.
lines.refuse: That is no medicine, dear, it is only a thing.
lines.purse_empty: I've spent all I had. Come back when someone has paid me.
lines.sold_out: My shelves are bare, so go and get hurt somewhere else for a while.

reactions.line: I heard what you did for those folk, and kindness gets a kinder price here.

friend.counter: Down there {foes}. I'd take {take} if I were you, and I was very nearly you.
friend.name: Marta Venn
friend.title: Rat-Catcher and Apothecary
friend.lore: Marta Venn is a rat-catcher who carries fever cure in jars of green bile to the children of Saint Agatha's. She had set her own broken leg and was bleeding beside those jars when you found her, and since you staunched the wound she keeps an apothecary's stall as well.
friend.line: My leg's mended, and forty kids at Saint Agatha's got their fever cure. You get a friend's price, and don't argue.

armourer.name: Brannoc
armourer.title: Armourer
armourer.lore: Ulf Brannoc went down twenty years ago as armourer to the army of a king, and that army never came back up. He remained to mend whatever does return, and at that work he is very skilled, though he has little gift for idle talk.
armourer._doc_counters: A cold-iron charm now and then, and always when the Fair Folk are below ('counter_classes': a counter, domain_counters; slice 5).

lines.order_placed: Your {item} will be on my rack at the stall on floor {floor}.
lines.order_refund: There's no stall of mine below this one. Have your coin back.
greet: Twenty years I've waited for that army to come back up, so you'll have to do instead.
Show me the blade. Who sharpened this for you, a goat?
Rust is how metal gives up, and I don't let it.
lines.bought: Keep it oiled, for I'll know if you don't.
lines.sold: It's decent steel, and I expect that someone died holding it.
lines.broke: Steel costs money, so come back richer or bleed on someone else's anvil.
lines.refuse: I work in metal, and that is no metal.
lines.purse_empty: I've no coin left for buying, though I've plenty of hammer.
lines.sold_out: The racks are empty. Kill something that has a sword, and bring the sword here.

friend.counter: Scouts say {foes} past here, so take {take}, as the Legion would.
friend.name: Jory Pell
friend.title: Armourer
friend.lore: Jory Pell was a young soldier of the Legion who fled when his company was broken, and who went back at last for those that were left alive in the old granary. He is done with trembling and with soldiering, and he sells what arms his company has no more need of.
friend.line: I'm Pell, late of the Legion. I sell what my company doesn't need now, at a friend's price to the one who sent me back.

bookseller.name: Crispin Vellum
bookseller.title: Bookseller
bookseller.lore: Crispin Vellum is a scribe who copies the writing from the dungeon walls and sells it to all who will pay for words. He has been sneezing since the third floor and will not speak of it. He goes no deeper than the temple of Athena, for below it, he says, the walls begin to write back.

lines.counter: The walls below say {foes}, and I have {take} on the shelf. ACHOO! Your pardon.
greet: Speak quietly, please, for the books are sleeping.
Every wall down here is a page to one who can read, and for a fee I'll read it.
That spellbook once bit a man, but the price is fair.
lines.bought: Read it twice, and afterward read it again.
lines.sold: Oh, that's a good one. ACHOO! Your pardon, it's a good one.
lines.broke: Words may be cheap, but mine are not.
lines.refuse: I deal in words, and that has none in it.
lines.purse_empty: My purse is as empty as a blank page.
lines.sold_out: I have nothing left to sell you but advice, which is to read more.

friend.counter: I've mapped what lies below, where {foes}, and I'd carry {take}.
friend.name: Helena Marsh
friend.title: Cartographer and Bookseller
friend.lore: Helena Marsh had made maps for twelve years and never drawn a bad line until her arm was hurt in the dark. Since you gave her back the use of her pen she has gone on mapping these halls, and she sells books and scrolls beside her maps.
friend.line: Twelve years and never a bad line, and it's thanks to you that I can still hold the pen. You get a friend's price.

abyssal.name: Vesper
abyssal.title: Dealer in the Deep
abyssal.lore: No one knows what Vesper is, and none has seen it blink. It takes gold and buys curses, and it is so courteous in all its dealings that folk fear it the more.

lines.counter: Down there {foes}, darling, so you will want {take}.
greet: How lovely it is to have a customer with a pulse.
All that you see belonged to someone braver than you, and is priced accordingly.
I buy curses, darling, and most gladly the ones that bite.
lines.bought: It suits you, as most things do for a little while.
lines.sold: Mm, it remembers its last owner. I do like that in a thing.
lines.broke: Oh dear, is this poverty? I have heard of it.
lines.refuse: No, I think not, darling, for I have taste.
lines.purse_empty: I have spent all that I care to on you today.
lines.sold_out: It is all gone. I do love a wholehearted customer.

reactions.line: You are so generous that I shall very generously charge you more.

sutler.name: Old Mags Thorn
sutler.title: Sutler
sutler.lore: Old Mags Thorn is a sutler, one of those who follow an army and sell it what it needs, save that she follows heroes down to the gates, for heroes pay best on the night before a fight. She has buried many customers and kept the deposit of each. She will go as far as Medusa's gate and not one stair further, since below it, she says, nobody comes back to pay.

gate_lines.19: Asterion's below, with a bull's head, a man's temper and a maze he knows by heart. Buy healing, and buy string if you can find it.
gate_lines.39: Medusa's below, and I mean it when I say don't look at her. The last lad who looked is my coat rack now. This is my last camp, for past her it's dwarves and worse.

lines.counter: Past this camp {foes}, so buy {take} or else buy a coffin.
greet: This is the last stall before the gate, and my prices are fairer than most heroes.
Buy now, for the dead can't haggle and you might be dead by teatime.
lines.bought: Good, you are a little less likely to die now.
lines.sold: I'll take it, and if you don't come back up I shall take the rest as well.
lines.broke: No money? Then you had better be very good at sums.
lines.refuse: I could never sell that on to anyone with sense.
lines.purse_empty: My purse is empty, but give it a day and somebody's deposit will come in.
lines.sold_out: You've cleaned me out, so go on now and be a legend.

reactions.line: I heard what you did for those folk, and Mags will remember.

regin.name: Regin
regin.title: Smith of Hreidmar's House
regin.lore: Regin is Fafnir's own brother, a dwarf and a smith. When their father Hreidmar took a ransom of gold for his third son, Otr, he would not share a coin of it. For this Fafnir killed him and lay down upon the gold until he became the worm below, and Regin had nothing. He reforged the sword Gram for the hero Sigurd and told him to dig a pit in the dragon's path, but the saga tells how the birds revealed to Sigurd what Regin meant to do when his brother was dead.

gate_lines.59: My brother takes the same track down to the water every day. Dig a pit in it and lie there, and drive up under his left shoulder as he crawls over you. That is all that you, or anybody else, will ever need to know.

lines.counter: Below us {foes}. Take {take}, for a smith knows what kills what.
greet: I am Hreidmar's other son, the one who didn't get the gold.
I sell steel, mail and a good edge, all a hero needs to kill a dragon, as I have cause to know.
My brother was a dwarf once, before the gold made a worm of him.
lines.bought: Good, now go down and use it on him.
lines.sold: I'll melt it down, for in a hot enough fire all things melt, as my brother could tell you.
lines.broke: There's no steel without gold, by our family's rule.
lines.refuse: That's no use to a smith.
lines.purse_empty: My purse is empty, though my brother's is not.
lines.sold_out: The racks are bare, for all that I had is going down that stair with someone.

reactions.line: I hear you told two quarrelling dwarves my father's story, so you know mine as well. My prices will be honest, and my hands will stay where you can see them.

tyr.name: Tiw
tyr.title: One-Handed Soldier
tyr.lore: An old soldier who calls himself Tiw keeps the last camp before the wolf, and his right hand is gone at the wrist, by a clean and very old bite. He laid it once in a wolf's mouth as a pledge that he knew would be broken, and he will tell you that he knew the price before ever he paid it. The English named Tuesday for a god of that name. He fed the wolf when it was a pup and the others were afraid to go near it, and no one has ever called him a peacemaker.

gate_lines.79: He lies on his island below, bound with a ribbon the dwarves made from six things that are not. It held when no chain would, so gather the six and bind him again.

lines.counter: On the road down, {foes}. Take {take}, for fair's fair.
greet: Sit and eat, for the wolf will keep.
I fed him when he was a pup and the others were afraid to, and later he took my hand for it. I call that fair.
Ask me anything you like but what happened to the hand.
lines.bought: A good choice, for you'll want it on the island.
lines.sold: I'll take it, for a soldier never has too many of those.
lines.broke: You have no coin, so fight well and come back with some.
lines.refuse: It's no use to me, or to anyone on that island.
lines.purse_empty: I have no more to give, for I gave the best of it a long time ago.
lines.sold_out: That is all I have. Go on down, for he is waiting and never liked to wait.

reactions.line: I hear you've an eye for a god in a beggar's coat, so you know whose camp this is. Keep it to yourself, and you shall pay what things are worth.

dwarf_armourer.name: Brunhild Irontemper
dwarf_armourer.title: Dwarf Smith
dwarf_armourer.lore: Brunhild Irontemper is a dwarf of the deep forges and of the honest kind, for when Fafnir's gold came among her people and half of them went wrong, she turned to her work. Dwarves made Thor's hammer, Odin's spear and the ribbon that holds the wolf, and she will tell you of all three while she mends your mail. For her work she will charge you what it is worth and not a coin more.

lines.counter: Down there {foes}, so take {take}, and keep the edge off stone.
lines.order_placed: You have paid fair. Your {item} will be on my rack at the stall on floor {floor}.
lines.order_ready: Here's your {item} as ordered, dwarf work and worth the wait.
lines.order_refund: I've no stall below this one, and a fair price means you get it back.
greet: Your weapon looks a little sad, doesn't it? I can fix that for a fair price.
The ribbon that holds the wolf was dwarf work, and so is everything on this rack.
Rust is metal that has stopped caring, so I do the caring for it.
lines.bought: Keep the edge off stone, for it is no pick.
lines.sold: It's good steel, badly kept. I'll put it right and sell it to someone kinder.
lines.broke: My price is a fair one, and a fair price has to be paid.
lines.refuse: I'll take steel, but that is no steel.
lines.purse_empty: My purse is empty but my anvil isn't, so bring me work, not wares.
lines.sold_out: The rack's bare, so go and break something, then bring it back for me to mend.

friend.counter: Father always said to know what's below. Down there {foes}, so take {take}.
friend.name: Frida
friend.title: Smith's Daughter
friend.lore: Frida is a dwarf and a smith's daughter, and for days she kept her hand upon the chest of her dead father, for she would not share it with her brother Hepti. When you had told her what Hreidmar's gold did to his children she lifted her hand, and now she trades with her share of her father's tools.
friend.line: Hepti filled his trench in and I took my hand off the lid, and we split Father's tools as well. You'll have a friend's price, since it was you who told us about Otr.

ghost_bookseller.name: Quentin Shelfmark
ghost_bookseller.title: The Cataloguer
ghost_bookseller.lore: Quentin Shelfmark came down a hundred years ago to copy the writing from the walls, as Crispin Vellum does now, and somewhere past Medusa's gate he died at the work and did not leave off working. He puts a label on all things, on walls and torches, on rats and on you, and he orders his catalogue as Callimachus ordered that of the great Library of Alexandria in a hundred and twenty rolls, first by subject and then by author. When you pay him, the coins fall through his hands into a box, and he files them under the letter G.

lines.counter: Below, {foes}. It is catalogued, and filed beside it under Remedies is {take}.
greet: A customer, encountered at last! Do hold still while I label you.
Everything down here is in my catalogue, first by subject and then by author, and you are under Visitors.
Mind the rat, for he is catalogued and I should hate to start again.
lines.bought: I strike it from the catalogue. Read it before something else does.
lines.sold: Oh, I have no copy of that one. How lovely to have a new shelfmark!
lines.broke: No coin? I shall file you under Browsers.
lines.refuse: That has no words in it, and I catalogue only words.
lines.purse_empty: My purse is empty, for money goes straight through me, I'm afraid.
lines.sold_out: There's nothing left on the shelves. Do come back when you've found me something to read.

friend.counter: I have seen what lies below, dear, where {foes}, and you will want {take}.
friend.name: The Sibyl of Cumae
friend.title: Seller of Books
friend.lore: The Sibyl of Cumae was granted as many years as there are grains in a handful of dust, but she forgot to ask for youth, and she withered until a bottle could hold her. Sooner than lower her price she burned six of her nine books of all that is to come, and she has not forgotten that you paid it for the last three.
friend.line: It is the same price as before, dear. No, for you a little less, since you paid the first time, as nobody ever does.

damned_generalist.name: Ortolan
damned_generalist.title: The Last Merchant
damned_generalist.lore: Ortolan kept a shop in a city above and never gave a beggar so much as a crumb from his table, and he keeps his shop still. As he counts his coins they melt between his fingers, and the chest on which he sits is warm because of where it stands. He has tried to leave off trading and cannot, for wherever a customer goes in the Abyss his shop is there before him. Jesus told of treasure laid up on earth, where moth and rust corrupt and thieves break through and steal, and all three have found their way among the wares of Ortolan.

lines.counter: Down there {foes}. I have {take}. I always have what you need, though it never helps.
greet: Welcome to Ortolan's Emporium, the deepest shop in the world, established longer than you've been alive!
Buy something, please, for I can't stop selling and nobody ever comes.
Pay the coins no heed, for they always do that.
lines.bought: Sold, and it doesn't help me. Selling never helps.
lines.sold: I'll buy it, as I must, for trade is all I'm allowed now.
lines.broke: No coin? I know how that feels, with a full chest and not a coin I can keep.
lines.refuse: Even down here I have standards, and they are all I have left.
lines.purse_empty: My purse is empty. It is always empty and always full, which is hard to explain.
lines.sold_out: There's nothing left, so come back tomorrow. My trouble is that here there is always a tomorrow.

reactions.line: So you pay other people's debts? I never did, and you'd think I'd have learned by now. Prices are up.
